full_judgment: confusion in that centre; that law and order broke down, and as such the election could not be held smoothly and some unruly persons also snatched away some ballot papers and cast illegal votes, which were counted illegally; that after filing the said election case, the petitioner, filed an application praying or temporary, injunction restraining the opposite party No. Md. Lutfar Rahman the newly elected chairman from taking oath and charge of the office of the Chairman of the Nazirpur Union Parishad upon which the Tribunal issued a show cause notice and passed an order of ad interim injunction in favour of the petitioner. Thereafter the Respondent opposite party No.1 appeared and filed a written objection and prayed for vacating the ad-interim order of temporary injunction Accordingly the said order of ad-interim injunction was vacated by the Tribunal on 29.9.88. Meanwhile, the Election Tribunal case was made ready for hearing, but having no appearance on behalf of the Respondent-opposite-party on the date of hearing, the same was taken up for ex-parte disposal on 13.11.88. The learned Election Tribunal Judge heard the case ex-parte and allowed the same and set aside the election of the Chairman of the said Union Parishad as illegal and void by her judgment and order dated 13.11.88. Being aggrieved by the said ex-parte order, the Respondent-opposite-party No.1 preferred an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No.51 of 1988 (Election) to the Appellant Tribunal (District Judge) Natore on 15.11.88. The appeal was admitted for hearing and the operation of the impugned ex-parte order was stayed till disposal of the appeal. Meanwhile the Deputy Commissioner, Natore directed the petitioner to make over charge of the office of the Chairman to the opposite-party No.1 Md. Lutfar Rahman, the elected chairman of the Nayirpur Union Parishad. Being aggrieved by that the petitioner filed a suit being O.C. Suit No. 108 of 1988 on 15.11.88 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Guruduspur who is also the Election Tribunal praying for a decree for permanent injunction restraining the opposite party No.1 from taking over charge of the. office of the Chairman from him and also filed an application for an order of ad-interim injunction to that effect,  The learned Assistant Judge on the said application passed an order dated 19.11.88 issuing a notice upon the defendant-opposite-parties No.1-6 to show cause as to why an order of temporary injunction as prayed for should not be granted against them and also directed them to maintain status quo in the meantime. The after, an application was filed by the defendant-opposite-party No.1 on 21.11.88 for vacating the order of injunction i.e. status quo and the same was fixed for hearing on 24.11.88. The learned Assistant Judge heard both the sides and disposed of the said application by observing that as the subject matter of the suit and that of the Election Tribunal Case is similar and related to each other and as the records of the Election Tribunal case have been attached with that of the Other Class Suit No. 108 of 1988 in compliance with an order of the learned Appellate Tribunal district Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal No.51 of 1988, it would not be proper to pass any new order in the said application. Being aggrieved by the said order dated 24.11.88 of the learned Assistant Judge, the defendant opposite party No. 1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 54 of 1988 before the learned, District Judge (Appellant Tribunal), Natore. When the said appeal came up for hearing analogously with Misc. Appeal No.51 of 1988, it appears that it was contended on behalf of the defendant appellant that the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in not holding that the Other Class Suit No. 108 1988 was not at all maintainable in law, in view of Section 26 of the Local Government (Union Parishads) Ordinance, 1983 (Ordinance No.51 of 1983) and as such no temporary injunction or even status quo could be granted by the learned Assistant Judge. On the other hand, it was submitted on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent that the suit was quite maintainable, but the instant appeal against the impugned order dated 24.11.88 was not at all maintainable. The learned District Judge (Appellate Tribunal) on consideration of the submissions and the materials on record allowed the appeal i.e. Misc. Appeal No.54 of 1988, set aside the order dated 24.11.88 and also dismissed the suit being O.C. Suit No.108 of 1988 as being not maintainable, by his judgment and order dated 18.1.89. Being aggrieved by this, the plaintiff-petitioner has moved this revisional application in this Court.
